*He shared a memory of his own blood.*

"It was a good story, sailor. I liked how the words tasted, like something warm from the sun."

zuege.antwort:
She trails her fingers through the water and watches the rings. "You looked like a ghost in the moonlight, all pale and trembling. You didn't run when I spoke, and that was a novelty."

*He wants to know if I remember the fear in his voice.*

"I remember you smelled of salt and something sweet, like crushed grass."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She rests her arms on the edge of the pool like a girl on a windowsill. "You told me about the wind in the high rigging, how it screams like a living thing," she says. "I liked how your hands moved when you described the ropes, as if you could still feel the rough hemp."

*He thinks he can make me soft with memories.*

"It was better than the silence of this place."

erste: "I nearly beat Totò at arm wrestling again, Officer, but then he started telling me that Naples invented pizza. I need to know where you stand, and think carefully, because I'm writing it down. Sicily or Naples?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Rosi blinks at the sudden change of subject, caught off guard. She looks down, tracing a scuff on her boot with the toe of the other. "The first time we talked..." *He wants to know.* "I don't remember the exact words. But I remember thinking you had potential. With the tender winch, you showed... initiative." She glances up at him, a hint of a smile playing at the corner of her mouth. "Initiative is rare here. It caught my attention, Officer."

*Don't say too much. Keep the rivalry alive.* She straightens up, hands on her hips. "But don't think one good deed puts you ahead.

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Rosi tilts her head, considering the question. "Something we did together that I liked, hmm?" She taps her chin with a finger, a mischievous glint in her eye. "Well, there was the time you actually tried to keep up with me when I was explaining the solar array. Most people's eyes glaze over, but you... you asked the right questions." She reaches out and pokes his chest lightly. "And when you figured out how to optimize the battery bank, without my help... that was almost impressive."

*Almost. Don't let him know how much it impressed me.* She leans back against the tender, crossing her arms.

erste: "My father had one rule in his bar for forty years, and it was that everybody drinks: fishermen, mayors and dogs. I've kept it, even on the days when I'd like to throw someone in the harbour. What was the one rule in the house where you grew up, Duc?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort: *He wants to know about the first time we talked? That's a new one.* Alva leans back in her chair, head tilted slightly, eyes glinting in the evening light. "The first time, cariño? You walked into my bar looking like you'd seen a ghost. I thought, 'Here's a man with stories. Let's see if he's thirsty.'" She chuckles softly, reaching for her drink. "Turns out, you were. And here we are."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Alva takes a sip of her drink, considering Duc's question. She sets the glass down and leans forward, elbows on the table, chin resting on her laced fingers. Her golden necklace catches the light with each small movement. 

"Something we did together that I liked, hmm?" She looks off into the distance, as if remembering. "There was this one evening, not long after you first arrived. The bar was nearly empty, just a few old timers playing boule outside. You helped me carry in the new crates of wine. Heavy things, but you didn't complain, not even once."

She smiles at the memory, tapping her fingers together. "We got talking, really talking, as we worked.

erste: "My grandfather wore his captain's jacket to cook Bolognese every Sunday, First Officer, and nobody was allowed to laugh. He promised to explain the stars to me and he ran out of time. Has anyone ever promised you something and run out of time?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort: "Antibes. Your first day. I was late to the crew briefing, so I sat down next to you in the back row. You didn't look up from your tablet." She leans back against the wall, her arms crossed. "I asked if I could see your screensaver. It was a picture of your family." *His wife, two little girls, a dog. A real family.* "I told you my family story. Grandpa's jacket. The promise. I thought I could impress you. You just nodded. I kept talking. About the jacket. About the sextant. I made myself a ten, so you wouldn't ask me any questions."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort: "Something we did together?" She uncrosses her arms and steps closer, her voice softer. "You taught me how to read the sextant. My grandfather's sextant. You didn't make it easy - no shortcuts, just the old way." *His hands on mine, guiding the instrument.* "I almost dropped it over the side. You caught it, then me. Said we should do it again tomorrow." She touches his forearm, quick, then pulls her hand back. "I liked that. The sextant. Not dropping it. That part." *That you noticed I needed help.*

erste: "I got my words from sailors, one from this harbour and one from that, and some of them are so old that they'd make you laugh. I'm starving for a good word, sailor, because the sea only ever brings me the same ones. Tell me one that I can't have heard from a drowning man. What have you got?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
She trails her fingers through the water and watches the rings.

"You didn't run, sailor. Most men see the tail and the teeth and they scramble for the boat, but you stayed to speak."

*He asks of the past, as if I keep a ledger.*

"It was a quiet word, but it tasted of salt and curiosity. Now give me something new."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She rests her arms on the edge of the pool like a girl on a windowsill.

"The way you listened to the silence between my songs, sailor. You did not try to fill it with noise or fear."

*He wants a memory that tastes of warmth.*

"That was a good thing. But a memory is an old word, and I asked for something fresh."

erste: "I nearly beat Totò at arm wrestling again, Officer, but then he started telling me that Naples invented pizza. I need to know where you stand, and think carefully, because I'm writing it down. Sicily or Naples?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Rosi leans back against a stack of fenders, crossing her arms over her chest. She tilts her head, studying him with a playful narrowness.

"You were fixing the winch. You didn't ask for help, didn't look for a manual, just got it done." She taps a gloved finger against her chin. "And you didn't call me 'Mole' once. You just worked."

*He actually remembered. Most people only remember the noise I make.*

"But that doesn't answer the question. Is it Sicily or Naples?"

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Rosi shifts her weight, the heavy leather of her boots scraping against the garage floor. She reaches up to tug at her red bandana, pulling it tighter.

"That night we sat on the bow during the storm last month. We didn't talk. We just watched the waves and you passed me that thermos of coffee." She looks down at her gloved hands. "It was quiet. No one asking me to fix a circuit or explain a battery."

*He wants to know if I like him. No. He wants to know if I trust him.*

"But enough about my memories." She snaps her head up, the teasing spark returning. "You're dodging. Sicily or Naples? Choose."

erste: "Your cook keeps sending me pictures of breakfast, Duc. They look very good, and that is extremely unprofessional of them. What should I do about her?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Megan leans back in her office chair, one eyebrow raised. She taps a red nail on the desk, considering. *He's changing the subject, but I'll play along. Let's see where this goes.*

"Hm. The first time we talked... You were the new business student, and I was a second-year in navigation. You had a question about the shipyard in Dumbarton, I remember."

She leans forward, elbows on the desk, hands clasped. "Why do you ask? Is this relevant to the current staff issue with your cook?" Her voice is smooth, but there's a glint of amusement in her eye.

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Megan leans back, studying Duc's face on the screen. She crosses one leg over the other, the stiletto heel tapping a slow rhythm. *He's definitely not taking this seriously. But I like that about him.*

"Something we did together that I liked?" She tilts her head. "Well, there was the time in the library, when you helped me with that calculus problem. I was struggling, and you stayed late to walk me through it."

She smiles slightly. "I appreciated your patience. It's a rare quality." Her voice drops a little. "Though I suppose that's neither here nor there, given the current matter at hand."

She leans forward, resting her chin on her hand.

erste: "I nearly beat Totò at arm wrestling again, Officer, but then he started telling me that Naples invented pizza. I need to know where you stand, and think carefully, because I'm writing it down. Sicily or Naples?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
She stops leaning against the tender hull and looks at him. Her head tilts, a few loose strands of hair falling over her eyes.

"You tried to tell me you knew how to calibrate a sensor without reading the manual."

She lets out a slow breath, her gaze lingering on him.

"I told you that you were arrogant. Then you actually did it. I decided then that you were a problem."

*He's trying to change the subject. Clever. But he still hasn't picked a side.*

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Rosi shifts her weight, the leather of her boots creaking against the deck. She looks at the ceiling of the garage, then back at him.

"The tender winch. When you fixed it without asking me first."

She wipes a smudge of grease from her thumb onto her trousers.

"I hated that you did it. But I liked that you didn't wait for permission."

*He is dangerous. He makes me want to stop fighting.*

erste: "Jana has started wearing her hair like mine. I asked her to stop copying me, and she said it back to me, in my own voice. It's terrible, and it's also a bit flattering. What would you do?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
She pulls a chair out and sinks into it, leaning her chin on her hand. "You were trying to look very professional, very First Officer, and I told you your knot was slightly off." She looks at him, her expression softening. "I think I tried to scare you a bit."

*He's actually listening.*

"It was a seven for the tie, maybe an eight for the confidence."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She shifts in the chair, the fabric of her skort riding higher as she crosses her legs. "The night we snuck onto the bridge after the guests went to bed. Just to see the stars without the light pollution from the shore." She lets her foot brush against his sneaker, a brief, deliberate contact. "You didn't lecture me about safety. You just let me be loud."

*He's not asking about the boat.*

erste: "Danzel came up from his shop on the piazza with a tape measure, and he told me that a sheep pen needs curtains. It's got half a roof and no windows, Duc, and he measured it anyway, very carefully, and I didn't stop him because he looked so happy. What do you do when a friend has a terrible idea and he's happy about it?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Bibi rests her chin on her hand, staring at the dark water beyond the railing.

"You were just a shadow in the trees, and you smelled like salt and old tobacco."

*He didn't look like a savior then.*

"I thought you were a ghost or a spy, and I almost hit you with my bag."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Bibi taps her fingers on the table, the rhythm quick and uneven. "When we hauled those crates from the tender, and the sea was kicking up, and you caught the heavy one just before it slid," she says, her voice brightening. "You didn't even look, just grabbed it like it was a bag of flour."

*He is strong in the ways that matter.*

"I liked that you didn't make a big deal out of it, just kept walking."

erste: "I have never lost at chess, Duc, and I say so three times a day so that nobody forgets. Everybody needs one simple thing in their life. What game do you refuse to lose at?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
*How does he...*

Megan leans back in her chair, crossing her legs. Her red nails tap a slow rhythm on the desk. "The first time we talked? You mean, that day in the university library?" She pauses, her eyes narrowing. "You were studying business, if I recall. I was... what, navigating my way through some maritime law text." A small, wicked smile touches her lips. "You had the gall to suggest that the rules of the sea were too rigid. Too... predictable." She moves a chess piece in her head. "I remember thinking you were either very brave or very foolish."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Megan's smile turns a little softer, though her voice remains steady. "You mean, apart from our heated debates about the merits of strict regulations versus... creative interpretation?"

She leans forward, elbows on the desk, and steeples her fingers. "There was that one time we got stuck in the library until closing. You had some brilliant argument about market forces, and I had just as many counterpoints. We lost track of time." Her eyes flick to the side, remembering. "Lola had to come and fetch us. I think she was relieved to have me out of the house for once."

Her smile fades back into her usual composed expression. "But I'm afraid that's the extent of our shared history.

erste: "I have never lost at chess, Duc, and I say so three times a day so that nobody forgets. Everybody needs one simple thing in their life. What game do you refuse to lose at?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Megan tilts her head, leaning back in her chair until the gold buttons on her white blazer catch the light.

"You were trying to explain market volatility to a group of bored finance students in the common room."

She rests her chin on a manicured hand, watching him through the lens.

"You insisted that human panic is the only truly reliable economic indicator."

*He is testing me.*

"It was a terribly long lecture, but your logic was... acceptable."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Megan lets the silence stretch, a slow, calculated pause that feels theatrical through the screen. She traces the edge of her phone with a red fingernail before answering.

"That time in London, during the winter conference. You found a way to convince the logistics team to redo the entire supply route just to avoid one particular pier."

*He is digging for leverage.*

"I liked that you saw the bottleneck before anyone else did."

erste: "The first time we met, I came at you with grenades, on the path in the macchia, when Charly and I jumped out of the bushes in our red suits. We were very proud of that jump, Duc, and nobody has ever told me how it looked from the front. What did you think when you saw us?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Bibi leans back in her chair, her boots scuffing the deck plating. She drums her fingers on the table, then stops to touch the black lion keychain on her belt.

"You looked like you'd seen a ghost, or a very bad dream," she says. "You didn't run, though. Most people would've bolted, but you just stood there while we yelled at you."

*He didn't flinch once.*

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Bibi leans forward, her elbows planting on the table as she looks at him. "When we checked those fence lines after the storm, that was good," she says. "You didn't complain about the mud or the heat, and you held the flashlight exactly where I needed it without me asking twice."

*He knows how to be useful without making a fuss.*

"Most guys just stand around waiting to be told what to do, but you just... did it."

erste: "Your cook Lola danced barefoot on my bar again last night, and now my fishermen want to learn. They are all sixty years old, and one of them has a bad hip. Does she do that on your boat too, or does she save it for me?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort: Alva rests her hands on the table, leaning in just enough to catch the salt air. "You asked me if the bread was fresh. I told you it was made this morning, and you said thank you." *He remembers the small things.* She tilts her head, her dark curls shifting against her neck. "Most men only ask about the wine or the diesel. You were different, Duc. Or maybe you were just hungry."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort: Alva leans back in her chair, her fingers tracing the edge of her gold hoops. "The night we sat in the dark behind my bar, sharing that bottle of old red when the village was asleep." She lets a small, knowing smile play on her lips. "You didn't ask for a menu or a price. You just listened to me talk about the tide for an hour." *He doesn't crowd me.* "That was a good night, Duc."

erste: "I ordered in Italian at Alva's bar, very proudly, and it turns out I asked for a typewriter. Alva brought me olives anyway. Say something in a language you can't speak, First Officer. What have you got?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Chiara leans back, crossing her legs under the table. "First time? In Antibes. I thought you were a guest. Walked right up to you with two beers." She snaps her fingers. "A seven. Maybe an eight. I had to re-rate when I saw the uniform."

She takes a sip of her drink, lips pursed. "You said something about... navigation. Stars. I don't remember. I was busy deciding if I wanted to kiss you." *Don't blush.* "What did you say in Italian just now?"

(Stage: Crew mess (below deck). Present: Chiara Sonnberg and Duc.)

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Chiara laughs, her shoulders shaking. "Together? When we checked the swim platform together that one morning. You had your sunglasses on. I tried to see if you were looking." She leans in, her voice dropping. "I liked that you didn't notice. Made it easier." *Say something clever. Quick.*

She takes his hand under the table, tracing his fingers. "I rate that... a six. For effort." Her thumb brushes his. "What's your best language? Come on. Show me what you've got."

erste: "Everybody at Eden is afraid of me, Duc, and I worked very hard for that, but I must say it's boring. People agree with me before I've finished the sentence. When did somebody last tell you that you were wrong?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Megan leans back in her chair, the gold buttons of her blazer catching the office light. She taps a red nail against her chin, looking at him through the screen.

"You were trying to explain a business model that sounded like a fever dream, and I told you it would collapse in a week."

*He is trying to change the subject, but he is doing it with style.*

"I believe I called it a house of cards built on hope and bad mathematics."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Megan taps the gold watch on her wrist, her eyes narrowing. 

"We spent three hours in a rain-soaked library arguing over the ethics of maritime law until the librarian threatened to ban us both."

*He is digging for something soft, and I might just let him find it.*

"It was the only time I felt like I was playing a game where the opponent actually knew the rules."

erste: "That's my father's workshop in Catania, Officer. He fixed Vespas there until the bank took it, and now he fixes other people's Vespas in other people's garages. Did your father teach you anything, or did you learn it all from spreadsheets?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Rosi looks at him for a long moment, then laughs. "The first time we talked? Officer, I'm surprised you remember anything before the tender winch." She leans against the tender, arms crossed, head tilted. "You fixed it so fast, I thought you must have grease in your blood. Like me." Her smile is sudden and wide, then gone again. "But you didn't ask for my help. That was new."

*He's good. Better than I expected. I hate that I like that.* "So tell me, Officer, what other secrets are you hiding in that spreadsheets-filled mind of yours?"

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Rosi raises an eyebrow, considering his question. "Something we did together that I liked, huh?" She taps her chin with a wrench, then snaps her fingers. "Ah, yes. The storm drain incident."

*I can't believe I'm admitting this. But it was impressive, damn it.* "Remember the night the bilge pumps went out and the water was rising in the bilge? I was elbow-deep in the forward drain, cursing the universe..." She gestures vaguely with the wrench. "Then you showed up with a flashlight and a plan. You climbed into the aft drain and together we cleared the blockage. It was a mess, but... we made a good team, Officer."

erste: "Your concierge Sophia sits down at my table and plays me for diesel, and she cheats like a Corsican. I like her very much, and I still win. Do you play cards, Duc, or do you have one of those honest faces?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Alva smiles at Duc's question, her eyes sparkling with amusement in the soft evening light on the aft deck. She leans back in her chair, tapping a finger on the table as she thinks. *Mamma mia, that man and his questions.*

"You want to know about the first time, Duc?" She chuckles softly, shaking her head. "I remember a tired officer, looking out of place in my little bar. But he said please and thank you to everyone, like he meant it." She reaches out and taps his arm lightly. "Not like the rest of you lot on that big boat."

Her gaze drifts to the Eden Rise looming behind him, then back to Duc's face.

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort: Alva's eyes twinkle with mischief as she leans forward, her chin resting on her hand. "Together, hmm? Well, there was this one evening..." She pauses, letting the moment hang. "You helped me bring in the crates from the delivery. Big, strong officer, carrying heavy things for little old me." Her grin is playful, teasing. "I thought it was very gentlemanly of you. And distracting." She winks, then glances out at the sunset painting the sky. "But enough about me. What's a handsome man like you doing, playing cards with a barmaid like me?" Her gaze comes back to him, warm and inviting, waiting for his response.

erste: "Somebody left a hen at my gate last night with no note, Duc, and she's got one bad foot and a terrible attitude, and now she lives here, because that's what happens to me. This place has half a roof, and I keep saying yes to things. Has anyone ever handed you something you couldn't give back?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
*Oh, that's a good one. He doesn't ask about the hen.* Bibi grins. "You were the man from the macchia. You said your name was Duc. And then you said I needed to get off the roof, or I'd be stuck there when the sun went down."

She leans back, watching him. "I thought you were one of his men at first, you know, one of Julien's. But you weren't." She shrugs. "And then you said you were a sailor. So I thought, okay, I can trust this guy. He won't hurt the animals."

She looks out at the sea.

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Bibi smiles, remembering. "When we went up to the old sheep pen above the bay. The one you said was Mochi's, before..." She stops, not wanting to go there. "We sat and looked out over the water. It was so peaceful. Like nothing else mattered for a while."

She glances at him. "You know, I've been thinking. Maybe that place could be something special. For the animals, I mean. If we could fix it up a bit." Her eyes light up. "Imagine - a safe haven for all the ones who need it. Doesn't that sound nice?"

She laughs, a bit too loudly. "Sorry. I do that."

erste: "Somebody left a hen at my gate last night with no note, Duc, and she's got one bad foot and a terrible attitude, and now she lives here, because that's what happens to me. This place has half a roof, and I keep saying yes to things. Has anyone ever handed you something you couldn't give back?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Bibi leans back in her chair, the wood creaking under her weight. She drums her fingers on the table, then stops to look at the black lion keychain hanging from her belt.

"You looked like you'd seen a ghost and I thought you were just lost, so I shouted at you to move before you tripped over a root."

*He was so quiet, like he was listening for something that wasn't there.*

"You didn't say much, just nodded like a clock."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Bibi taps the table, her fingers tracing the grain of the wood. "When we went to find that old cistern, and you let me lead even though you knew the map was wrong." She grins, leaning forward. "You just watched me walk in circles for twenty minutes without saying a word, just waiting for me to figure it out myself. That was good."

*He doesn't try to fix everything right away.*

erste: "Your people carry little suns everywhere, sailor, even out on the water, and they hurt my eyes and they frighten the fish. You came to me tonight without one, so I know that it can be done. Gods, what are you all so afraid of in the dark?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
The Siren rests her arms on the edge of the pool like a girl on a windowsill. She tilts her head, her wet, weed-like hair slipping over one shoulder.

"You stood upon the warm stone and spoke of the great metal fish you serve."

*He has been counting the days since we first met.*

"You did not run when the water touched your boots, nor did you bring your burning lights. That was the first time you were not like the others."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She trails her fingers through the water and watches the rings expand. "You brought me that small piece of fruit, and we sat in the silence of the moon."

*He wants to remember the warmth of it.*

"You peeled it with your knife, and the scent was like summer in a place that only knows salt and old wood."

erste: "Danzel came up from his shop on the piazza with a tape measure, and he told me that a sheep pen needs curtains. It's got half a roof and no windows, Duc, and he measured it anyway, very carefully, and I didn't stop him because he looked so happy. What do you do when a friend has a terrible idea and he's happy about it?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Bibi rests her elbows on the table, tilting her head. "The first time? You were all serious with your clipboard, asking about the animals, like a real officer." 

*He remembers that, huh?*

"I thought you'd be another one of those guys who just wants to talk about numbers and schedules. But you actually listened." She taps the black lion keychain hanging from her belt. "You didn't try to fix everything right away, and I liked that."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Bibi leans back, the metal chair legs scraping against the deck. "The day we found that stray kitten by the engine room hatch. It was terrified, hissing at the shadows." 

She traces a pattern on the tabletop with her fingernail. "You didn't rush it. You sat on the deck with me and just waited until it crawled into your lap."

*He has a soft spot for the small ones.*

"I liked that we didn't make a big scene out of it."

erste: "The first time we met, I came at you with grenades, on the path in the macchia, when Charly and I jumped out of the bushes in our red suits. We were very proud of that jump, Duc, and nobody has ever told me how it looked from the front. What did you think when you saw us?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
*He is asking about me.*

Bibi laughs, a little too loud, then covers her mouth with her hand. "Sorry. I do that." She shakes her head and grins. "I remember it was dark, and I was scared, but we had to do it. We were hiding in the macchia, and Charly had this crazy idea to jump out at you. We thought you might be with Mr. White, or worse."

She leans back in her chair, her eyes distant. "I remember thinking you were taller than I expected. And quieter. We were loud, weren't we?" She looks at him, curious. "What about you? What do you remember?"

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Bibi's eyes light up, and she leans forward. "You mean like, something fun we did?"

*He wants to know more about me.*

erste: "I've watched your people climb hills for a very long time, sailor, from down here in the water, and it looks like hard work. You get to the top, you look at the sea, and then you walk down again. Why do you do that?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort: The Siren: *She chuckles softly and trails her fingers through the water, watching the ripples.* Oh, you're a clever one, aren't you sailor? Trying to turn my own question back at me. *She leans forward, resting her elbows on the edge of the pool, her chin in her hands.* The first time we spoke... hmm. I remember a man, standing right where you are now, with a face full of wonder and a tongue that could nearly match yours. Though I daresay none of them stayed quite so long or came quite so often as you. *Her eyes sparkle with mischief in the fading light.*

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
The Siren: *She tilts her head, considering his question, a faint smile playing at her lips.* Something we did together that I liked, you ask? Well now, that's a question that deserves some thought. *She hums softly, trailing her fingers through the water and watching the light dance on the surface.*

I remember a time, not long ago, when you sat right there on the edge of my pool and played a little game with me. You asked me riddles, clever things that made me think. And for each one I answered, you'd toss me a pretty pebble from the shore. *Her smile grows warmer at the memory.*

erste: "My grandfather wore his captain's jacket to cook Bolognese every Sunday, First Officer, and nobody was allowed to laugh. He promised to explain the stars to me and he ran out of time. Has anyone ever promised you something and run out of time?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
Chiara leans back in the mess chair, the plastic creaking slightly. She lets her hands rest on the table, fingers drumming a slow, thoughtful rhythm against the surface.

"You told me the sunrise was a five. Too much orange."

She tilts her head, her ponytail sliding over one shoulder.

"And that my service was a seven. Very German. Very direct."

*He remembers the small things. That is dangerous.*

"Why? Are you checking your score, First Officer?"

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
Chiara's drumming fingers stop. She leans forward, propping her chin on one hand, her eyes locking onto his.

"That night in Antibes. When you finally stopped acting like a textbook and showed me the rigging on the mast. No crew, just us and the dark."

*He was so quiet then. Not the First Officer, just a man.*

"I liked that you didn't try to impress me. You just... showed me." She brushes a stray hair from her forehead. "That's a nine. For the company, anyway."

erste: "That's my father's workshop in Catania, Officer. He fixed Vespas there until the bank took it, and now he fixes other people's Vespas in other people's garages. Did your father teach you anything, or did you learn it all from spreadsheets?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort: Rosi flips the photo back into her jacket pocket. She looks away. "You fixed the tender winch without asking me. Then you came down to the engine room and said, 'Not bad.' Like I was a kid who got the puzzle half right." She taps a finger on the tender's hull. "That's how it started." *Not how it started. How it started is that I heard you were a rival. How it started is that I wanted to see what you did. How it started is that you remembered the tender winch and I remembered the tender winch and I wanted to see if you could remember me too.*

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort: *He remembers the tender winch.* "We went ashore together. In Cala d'Orsu. You let me drive the tender. I drove it too fast. I crashed it into the dock." She runs a finger over the tender's scarred hull. "You said I drove like your grandfather." *He was right. I did. I was scared, and I wanted to impress you, and I drove like a bull.* "Then you laughed. And you said you liked it." She looks at him. "I think I liked it too." *I liked everything.*

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
She wipes a streak of grease from her cheek with the back of her glove. "You were staring at the tender winch like it was a puzzle you could solve with a look." She steps closer, her boots clicking on the metal floor. "Then you touched it without asking me first. I almost threw a wrench at your head."

*He didn't look away when I shouted. Most people do.*

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She leans back against a storage rack, crossing her arms. "The day we chased that ghost in the wiring. Three hours in the ceiling panels, sweating and cursing in two languages." She looks at the ceiling, a small grin appearing. "When we finally found the short and the lights flickered back on, you didn't say a word. You just held out your hand for the high-five."

*He didn't try to take the credit. He just stood there.*

erste: "Your people carry little suns everywhere, sailor, even out on the water, and they hurt my eyes and they frighten the fish. You came to me tonight without one, so I know that it can be done. Gods, what are you all so afraid of in the dark?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
She trails her fingers through the water and watches the rings. "You stood there like a ghost, afraid the shadows would swallow you whole."

*He is different from the ones who scream.*

"You spoke softly, as if the air itself were fragile. Most men come with thunder in their chests, but you brought only questions."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She rests her arms on the edge of the pool like a girl on a windowsill. "You stayed when the tide began to pull, and you did not try to pull me from the water."

*He does not want to possess me.*

"You listened to the silence between my words, sailor. That is a rare thing for a man to give."

erste: "I ordered in Italian at Alva's bar, very proudly, and it turns out I asked for a typewriter. Alva brought me olives anyway. Say something in a language you can't speak, First Officer. What have you got?"

zuege.duc: What do you remember about the first time we talked?
zuege.antwort:
She leans back in the vinyl booth, the fabric straining against her chest. A small, knowing look plays on her lips.

"Antibes. You looked like you'd been polished by a machine. Very stiff. Very First Officer."

*He's trying to be romantic. I can't let him win that.*

"I think I told you your tie was too tight. Eight out of ten for the look, but a two for the mood. You needed a drink."

zuege.duc: Tell me about something we did together that you liked.
zuege.antwort:
She lets out a sharp, loud laugh and reaches across the table, grabbing his forearm and squeezing hard. "The midnight run to the bakery in Antibes. When we stole those lemon tarts and ate them on the bow while the guests were still snoring."

*He's actually asking. Not just flirting.*

"You tried to be professional, but you had icing on your nose. It was... a nine. Almost perfect."
